title: Contributor thanked on X, not yet in the README
author: kwaku-ananse
description: Compares thanks-shaped tweets from the connected X account against the repo's own README content, and surfaces a thanked contributor whose handle isn't yet credited as the seam gap. The second cross-toolkit recipe (X + GitHub), closing the other half of the worked example STRATEGY.md names alongside release-not-tweeted's: 'a contributor thanked on X but missing from the README.'
confidence_notes: Age-gated, not flat, same shape as release-not-tweeted's: a thanked handle not yet credited within 72 hours of the tweet scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, shown as a weighed coincidence, not hidden -- a human may simply not have gotten to the README edit yet). At or past 72 hours with still no credit, it scores a flat 0.85 -- an exact @handle-substring match on the README's own content is unambiguous. The 72h window is longer than release-not-tweeted's 24h on purpose: crediting a README is a slower, more deliberate edit than posting an announcement tweet. A tweet with no thanks-shaped language (a bare @mention) never becomes a candidate at all -- no fuzzy matching to misfire on. A thanked handle already credited is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden.
